en: The Exposition of the Face of the Yogāmbara.
NAK 4-258 = NGMPP 119/14 [1r] [Siddham]. Homage to the glorious Yogāmbara!
Having first prostrated to Nāgārjuna, I pay homage to the word of the Buddha, which begins with the four syllables and is both extremely manifest and profoundly secret. (1)
I bow to this secret region, the nectar-abode of the lotus, which was created from the reality of primordial wisdom—the first dharma. (2)
I bow to the speech of Vajracetas for the sake of reality, which, through the knowledge of the *ali*, is a lotus; it is honey, possessing the taste of nectar—this I honor with three words. (3)
She indeed awakens the pride of wrath and the gnosis of all beings;
through the tilaka of the path, I bow with these three words. (4)
I bow to the word of the Buddha, which is the supreme state of the three vehicles, the succession of births and non-births, and the aspiration of beings who have not yet crossed over. (5)

Having placed the offerings beginning with the fivefold service (pañcāpacāra) on the right side, the vessel for the water of honor (argha) and so forth on the left side, and having set out the sacrificial offering (bali).
The yogi, with a concentrated mind, visualizes a black vajra above the four mandalas in his heart, and at his throat, a black syllable Hrīḥ upon a lotus. Oṃ jihvāsaṃvartini hūṃ phaṭ.
Following that is the purification of the hands: *suṃ kṣuṃ yuṃ huṃ aḥ*. The right hand is *jñāna* (wisdom). *smryuṃ hmryuṃ ymryuṃ kṣmryuṃ saḥ*. The left hand is *vijñāna* (discriminative awareness).

Having pressed the lotus with knowledge, one should perform the eight-limbed placement (*aṣṭāṅgakaraṇa*) using the trident and the fingers on the hand: *suṃ* on the tongue; *kṣuṃ* on the head; *yuṃ* on the ears and nose; *hūṃ* on the eyes; *smryuṃ* on the throat; *hmryuṃ* on the two arms; *ymryuṃ* on the heart; *kṣmryuṃ* on the navel.
[1v] Following that, the empowerment of the three bodies: Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.
Then, [one should perform] the empowerment of all things with the Sattvavajrī mudrā: Oṃ smryuṃ sarvasaṃśodhanī hūṃ phaṭ.
Like the wings of a swan enveloped by wisdom and discernment. Oṃ vajrakavace hūṃ phaṭ. The stakes, the wall, and the cage for binding the directions are to be performed in their proper sequence.

The mudrā of Sattvavajrī is filled with the sound of the syllable *hūṃ*. With the earth-canopy encircled by lotuses, one should raise white *arocana* and rotate it as the *uṣṇīṣa*. On the crown, forehead, two ears, head, and back, there are five [deities] beginning with Vairocana in due order. *Oṃ hūṃ aḥ svāhā*. Having raised white *arocana* and rotated it by means of a knot, the mantra is *oṃ ṭaṭ*. With equal rhythm, *vajra tuṣya hoḥ 3*.

The yogi, well-composed and having placed [his gaze] on the tip of the nose, should visualize the mandala-circle: Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ | Oṃ ākarṣaya ni hūṃ | Oṃ āḥ pratīccha arghaṃ hūṃ | Oṃ pravarasatkārārghaṃ hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ pravarapādyaṃ pratīccha svāhā | Oṃ pravarācamanaṃ pratīccha svāhā | Vajrapāśa, Vajrasphoṭa, Vajrāveśa hoḥ | Oṃ supriye gandhe hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ śriyajapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā |

Oṃ aḥ vajradhūpe hūṃ svāhā || Oṃ kṣuṃ vajradīpe hūṃ svāhā || Oṃ guṃ svāhā || Oṃ i svāhā || [Offer] the bali and naivedya || One should present them with their respective mantras, as well as the eightfold worship beginning with lāsyā.

Welcome, O Dharma, free from affliction, stainless and devoid of impurity! Prostrate with devotion to that which is free from the grasp of grasping. Having seen the purified Dharma, there is indeed no conceptualization of Mount Meru; Brahmin, Kurukuru, and Caṇḍāla are of one single nature—[all are] a mere skeleton. *Oṃ*, the letter *A* is the mouth of all phenomena because they are unarisen from the beginning. *Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ*. Prostrate to the state, and you shall be liberated. There is no limb here that is not swift; it is the embrace of *Doṃ*, adorned by *Mā*.
Tenā hūṃ 2, tenā te te hūṃ.
The being without beginning or end, Vajrasattva of great bliss,
Samantabhadra, the self of all, the Lord of the Vajragarbha— [this is] the Vajra-reality.
Everything has the characteristic of space, and space itself is without characteristics;
through union with the equality of space, the equality of all that is supreme becomes manifest.

Oṃ vajra-ghaṇṭā-raṇita-praṇita sarvatathāgata-citta-saṃcodani, vajrasattva-hṛdayāvatāraṇi prajñāpāramitā-nāda-svabhāve āḥ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hoḥ ṭarkki jaḥ hoḥ iti. This is the reality of the bell (ghaṇṭā-tattva).
The Vajra ornament adorns [the body]; liberation saves the beings.
One should establish the liberation through Dharma as the task and maintain pure conduct.
"Haraṇimakuṭa," and so forth.

Then, preceded by the *kamalāvarta* gesture, one performs the salutation consisting of the five maṇḍalas: *Oṃ namas te hūṃ*, *Oṃ namo nama hūṃ*, *Oṃ namāmi hūṃ*. Having performed these three prostrations, one says: "You are the pledge (*samaya*), O pledge! Ho! Ho! Ho! I shall establish all beings in nirvāṇa. This is the commencement of the *Ādiyoga*.

The yogi, intent on his goal, sits in the sattvaparyaṅka posture. In his own heart, he visualizes the syllable *kṣuṃ*, blazing with the brilliance of fire, which melts his own body until it becomes as subtle as a hundred-thousandth part of the tip of a hair, illuminating [all]. He recites: *oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśuddho ’ham*.
In the absence of existence, there is no cultivation; for existent things, there is truly no cultivation.
Thus, existence would not arise from existence, and cultivation is not perceived.
One should say, "I am knowledge."
Oṃ, all phenomena are vajra-pure; I am vajra-pure.
Jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ! O Vajrasattva, may I attain the siddhi of causing [beings] to descend.
Ha ha ha ha hūṃ! I am the Lord of the Marvelous Arising, the Samaya of the Sound of Hūṃ.
Va va va vaḥ! You who possess a body arisen from the secret explosion of the vajra!
A A A A ĀḤ A HO! O you who sport with a single bee, HŪṂ! I am the one currently present.
Complete with all the auspicious marks and beautifully adorned with six arms.
With three faces displaying laughter, wrath, and passion, he possesses three eyes.
Meditating upon the Lord, the all-pervading one who is clothed in the yoga of the Buddhas, as he holds a vajra and a water-pot, a bell, a kama-club, and a vessel.

I am the arising Mahāmudrā, the mantra: *a ā ā ā āṃ*. One should apply [these] four heart-syllables to the heart, throat, and crown. The earth-parasol is consciousness, shaped like a chain; one should fashion it as white, smoke-colored, conch-white, yellow-ochre, and the three impurities, with a needle in the middle. *Oṃ samaya tiṣṭha svamī hūṃ svāhā*. Thus. *Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through yoga; I am pure through yoga.*
The *Devatāghorapañjikā*, known as the *Śrīyogāmbara-mukhākhyāna*, is completed.
By nature there are five transgressions, as well as those that are transgressions by convention;
whatever evil is of the body, whatever is likewise of the mind,
and whatever evil is of speech— all that you shall exhaust.
O Protector, standing before the Protectors, I shall confess;
with palms joined and full of devotion, I prostrate again and again.
This transgression has been transcended; therefore, may the Leaders accept it.
This was not auspicious, O Protector; it shall not be done by me again.
Whether it be deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, and likewise deficient in meditative cultivation, or even impure due to a lack of devotion— you shall consume all of that.
Neither from behind, nor by way of the path of memory, nor having entered into the application of subsequent discourse,
he has gone in every way for the sake of benefit.
The Kūrma school has four [recensions] consisting of happy combinations.

One should conceive of that which possesses the conduct of five colors through the distinction of various colors as being of a single color—non-conceptual and blue in form. This is the pledge (*samaya*).
